We propose lightweight tiny graph transformer network (TGTNet) models for classifying clutter from stationary and moving targets in the scene. Performance evaluation on the public RadarScenes show that our proposed TGTNet models achieve similar classification performance in precision and recall metrics in comparison to state of the art models, with one to two orders of magnitude lower model size and significantly faster inference.

AI.tldr: TGTNet is a lightweight tiny graph transformer that classifies automotive radar clutter from stationary and moving targets, matching state-of-the-art precision and recall on RadarScenes with one to two orders of magnitude smaller models and faster inference.
AI.motivation: Clutter, detections of non-existent moving objects in automotive radar, can degrade target detection and downstream driving decisions, and large models are costly for embedded use.
AI.method: The authors propose the tiny graph transformer network TGTNet to classify clutter versus stationary and moving targets in the scene.
AI.result: On the public RadarScenes dataset TGTNet achieves precision and recall similar to state-of-the-art models, with one to two orders of magnitude lower model size and significantly faster inference.
AI.conclusion: Compact graph transformers can handle radar clutter classification at a fraction of the cost of larger models.

title: An Agentic Framework for Quality-Aware and Scenario-Adaptive Image Compression
summary: Despite decades of progress, image codecs remain difficult to adapt to diverse real-world compression scenarios for two main reasons. First, most image codecs are optimized for a specific objective and require substantial redevelopment when the compression goal changes. Second, they typically assume clean inputs, whereas sensor-captured images often contain degradations that alter rate-quality behavior. To address these challenges, we propose Practical Image Coding Agents (PICA), a multi-agent framework that adapts existing codecs to diverse user requirements and potentially degraded inputs. PICA consists of four collaborative agents: a Perception agent that interprets user intent and analyzes image content, an Improvement agent that jointly considers bitrate and reconstruction quality to guide pre-coding restoration, a Coding agent that refines quality-control settings from global to regional levels, and an After-coding improvement agent that addresses residual degradations and compression-induced artifacts through restoration guided solely by image quality. To enable codec-agnostic regional adaptation, we introduce Agentic ROI Coding (AROIC), which treats the codec as a black box and allows the agent to automatically schedule, execute, evaluate, and reflect ROI coding plans without architectural modifications or codec-specific retraining. We integrate these four agents with a Scenario-Guided Quality-Rate (SGQR) evaluation strategy to enable more effective scenario-adaptive compression across heterogeneous codecs. Comprehensive experiments on clean, noisy, and blurred images across standard, perceptual, and machine-vision compression scenarios demonstrate that PICA consistently enhances the compression performance of both the conventional H.266/VVC codec and the neural Cheng2020 codec, outperforming competing compression methods on the Kodak, CLIC2020, and HEVC datasets.

AI.tldr: PICA is a multi-agent framework that adapts existing image codecs such as H.266/VVC and Cheng2020 to user requirements and degraded inputs via perception, improvement and coding agents, and an agentic ROI coding scheme that treats the codec as a black box.
AI.motivation: Image codecs are optimised for one objective and need redevelopment when the goal changes, and they assume clean inputs, whereas sensor images often contain degradations that alter rate-quality behaviour.
AI.method: Four agents (Perception, Improvement, Coding and After-coding improvement) work with Agentic ROI Coding, which schedules, executes and reflects on regional coding plans without codec modification, and a Scenario-Guided Quality-Rate evaluation strategy.
AI.result: PICA consistently enhances the compression performance of both H.266/VVC and the neural Cheng2020 codec on clean, noisy and blurred images across standard, perceptual and machine-vision scenarios, outperforming competing methods on Kodak, CLIC2020 and HEVC datasets; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Agentic adaptation of existing codecs offers a codec-agnostic route to scenario-adaptive and degradation-robust compression.

title: ProAlign: Progressive Positional and Prototype-Guided Alignment for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
summary: Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification (AG-ReID) aims to match pedestrian images captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and ground-based surveillance cameras. The task remains highly challenging due to severe viewpoint discrepancies, frequent occlusions, and substantial domain gaps between aerial and ground imagery. Beyond these observable factors, existing methods often overlook two fundamental structural issues: cumulative positional drift during hierarchical feature extraction and semantic inconsistency across cross-view feature distributions. To address these challenges, we propose ProAlign, a Progressive Positional and Prototype-Guided Alignment Network for AG-ReID. ProAlign comprises two key components: a Layer-wise Progressive Positional Embedding (LPPE) module and a View-Aware Prototype Contrastive Learning (PCL) module. LPPE performs adaptive positional calibration throughout transformer layers by employing conditional positional encoding in shallow layers to mitigate local spatial distortions, while introducing learnable static positional embeddings in deeper layers to reinforce global semantic priors. Meanwhile, PCL maintains view-specific aerial and ground prototypes for each identity and enforces cross-view semantic consistency via a dual-prototype contrastive objective. Extensive experiments on CARGO and two real-world AG-ReID benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of ProAlign, achieving state-of-the-art overall retrieval performance on CARGO with improvements of 1.60% in Rank-1 accuracy and 5.01% in mAP over the strongest competing methods.

AI.tldr: ProAlign improves aerial-ground person re-identification with layer-wise progressive positional embeddings and view-aware prototype contrastive learning, reaching state-of-the-art retrieval on CARGO with gains of 1.60% Rank-1 and 5.01% mAP.
AI.motivation: Aerial-ground person re-identification faces viewpoint discrepancy, occlusion and domain gaps, and existing methods overlook cumulative positional drift across transformer layers and cross-view semantic inconsistency.
AI.method: The Layer-wise Progressive Positional Embedding module uses conditional positional encoding in shallow layers and learnable static embeddings in deeper layers, and the View-Aware Prototype Contrastive Learning module keeps aerial and ground prototypes per identity under a dual-prototype contrastive objective.
AI.result: On CARGO ProAlign achieves state-of-the-art overall retrieval with improvements of 1.60% in Rank-1 and 5.01% in mAP over the strongest competing methods, and it is also evaluated on two real-world AG-ReID benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Progressive positional calibration and prototype-based cross-view alignment together improve aerial-ground person matching.

title: ScoreDial: Precise Control of Visual Attributes in Image Generation via Regressor Guidance from Limited Human Ratings
comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 37 pages, 27 figures, 4 tables, including the supplementary material
summary: Requested-value control is stricter than continuous steering: given $c$ on a human-rating scale, the generated image should attain that value from only limited ratings. We present ScoreDial, which fits a differentiable regressor $R$ to 100-479 human-rated images; once $R$ is fixed, a requested value $c$ is defined on its output scale, and learned target conditioning is paired with error-adaptive guidance that repeatedly reduces $|R(\mathbf{x})-c|$ during sampling. Across tire slip resistance, interior visual complexity, food desire-to-eat, and soap translucency, using one set of sampler settings shared across all four, ScoreDial reaches requested values and achieves, on all four attributes, $R$-MAE at most 0.013 over a range of width 0.8 and Spearman $\rho=0.980$, the maximum attainable under our evaluation protocol. Because $R$ also drives sampling, we evaluate agreement with $R$ separately from matched sweeps, an independent auditor fitted to the same ratings on a backbone none of the deployed regressors uses, and blinded human judgments. MPGD-flow also reaches the requested values under $R$, but ScoreDial has larger auditor displacement on every attribute, the largest among all compared methods, and a stronger MPGD-flow setting gives up target agreement without closing this gap. On every attribute, removing target conditioning leaves low $R$-MAE but more than halves auditor displacement, separating precise score correction from attribute movement. Blinded rating studies with 15 raters per attribute show that mean human ratings track $c$ on tire and soap, with linear $R^2=0.665$ and $R^2=0.786$, and in forced-choice comparisons of matched sweeps, raters chose ScoreDial's as the clearer progression in at least 84% of judgments against every baseline.

AI.tldr: ScoreDial gives precise requested-value control of image attributes by fitting a regressor to 100-479 human ratings and guiding sampling with error-adaptive correction, reaching R-MAE at most 0.013 and Spearman rho 0.980 across four attributes.
AI.motivation: Continuous steering does not guarantee that a generated image attains a requested rating value, and existing methods cannot reliably hit a specified value on a human-rating scale from limited ratings.
AI.method: A differentiable regressor R is fitted to a small set of human-rated images, learned target conditioning is paired with error-adaptive guidance that reduces |R(x) - c| during sampling, and one shared sampler setting is used for all four attributes.
AI.result: ScoreDial reaches requested values with R-MAE at most 0.013 over a range of width 0.8 and Spearman rho 0.980 on tyre slip resistance, interior visual complexity, food desire-to-eat and soap translucency; it has larger auditor displacement than MPGD-flow on every attribute, and blinded raters chose its sweeps as the clearer progression in at least 84% of judgements.
AI.conclusion: Target conditioning and score correction jointly give precise value control, but the attribute drift this entails is a trade-off the authors measure directly with an independent auditor.

title: Can saliency maps flag chest radiograph classifier errors at a new hospital? An external validation study
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, 6 Extended Data figures and 4 Extended Data tables. Code: this https URL
summary: Saliency maps are offered as a safeguard for medical image classifiers, but whether they reveal individual errors at a new hospital remains largely untested. We trained a convolutional network and a vision transformer on NIH ChestX-ray14 and evaluated 303,768 decisions per model at the training hospital and at two external sites, in the USA and Vietnam, with radiologist-consensus labels. We scored each explanation by its anatomical enrichment, the area-normalized concentration of attribution in a segmented thoracic region, and tested whether it detects errors beyond the model's confidence. Grad-CAM localized findings less often than radiologists (hit rate at most 0.575 versus 0.888). Adding enrichment to a confidence-based error detector calibrated at the training hospital never raised its area under the curve by more than 0.011, and for the convolutional network the relation between enrichment and correctness reversed between hospitals, degrading the transferred detector. Model confidence, not saliency, should anchor deployment monitoring.

AI.tldr: External validation on chest radiographs shows that saliency maps do not reliably flag classifier errors at new hospitals, and model confidence rather than saliency should anchor deployment monitoring.
AI.motivation: Saliency maps are offered as a safeguard for medical image classifiers, but whether they reveal individual errors at a new hospital has not been tested.
AI.method: A CNN and a vision transformer trained on NIH ChestX-ray14 were evaluated on 303,768 decisions per model at the training hospital and at two external sites in the USA and Vietnam, with radiologist-consensus labels, scoring explanations by anatomical enrichment and testing error detection beyond confidence.
AI.result: Grad-CAM localised findings less often than radiologists (hit rate at most 0.575 versus 0.888); adding enrichment to a confidence-based error detector never raised its AUC by more than 0.011, and for the CNN the enrichment-correctness relation reversed between hospitals, degrading the transferred detector.
AI.conclusion: Saliency does not add reliable error detection at new sites, so monitoring should rely on model confidence.

title: On the Learnability of Footwear Robustness: Footstep Recognition Under Unseen Conditions
summary: Footstep patterns, captured using pressure or force-sensitive walkways during natural walking, offer a convenient and passive approach to biometric recognition. However, footwear variability poses a major challenge to practical deployment, as it impacts both the foot-sensor interface and the user's underlying gait mechanics. This study considers the particularly difficult scenario where users enroll under one fixed footwear condition but must later be recognized in arbitrary, unseen footwear. Using the StepUP-P150 dataset, we show that footwear-induced shift, while substantial and heterogeneous across individuals, contains shared structure that can be learned from a training population and transferred, zero-shot, to previously unseen users and footwear styles. We do this using BiStepNet, a novel architecture that decomposes spatial and temporal identity cues into independently trainable streams and outperforms compact 3D spatiotemporal baselines for cross-footwear recognition. We demonstrate that cross-footwear recognition performance scales systematically with the volume and diversity of footwear representation in the training set, with gains transferring to footwear styles not directly observed during training. Moreover, we show that auxiliary gait datasets with only partial modality overlap (incorporated through the architecture's decomposed design) can be leveraged to further improve robustness to unseen footwear conditions.

AI.tldr: BiStepNet learns footwear-induced shift in footstep recognition so that users enrolled in one footwear can be recognised zero-shot in unseen footwear, with performance scaling with footwear diversity in training.
AI.motivation: Footwear changes both the foot-sensor interface and gait mechanics, which makes footstep biometrics hard to deploy when enrolment and later use involve different footwear.
AI.method: BiStepNet decomposes spatial and temporal identity cues into independently trainable streams, and auxiliary gait datasets with partial modality overlap are incorporated through the decomposed design; experiments use the StepUP-P150 dataset.
AI.result: BiStepNet outperforms compact 3D spatiotemporal baselines for cross-footwear recognition, performance scales systematically with the volume and diversity of footwear in training, the gains transfer to unseen footwear styles, and auxiliary datasets further improve robustness.
AI.conclusion: Footwear-induced shift contains learnable shared structure, so robust footstep recognition across footwear is feasible without enrolling in every footwear condition.

title: Manifold Embedding of Deep Image Features for Image Matching via Neural Adjoint Maps
summary: Estimating semantic correspondences between different object instances of similar categories in real-world images is a fundamental challenge in computer vision. While the recent progress in foundation models has significantly advanced solutions for such difficult image correspondence problems, respective methods are often insufficiently regularised. For example, common nearest-neighbour matching with foundation model features often results in noisy correspondences, which is particularly prominent when solving for dense correspondences. In this work, we tackle image matching via functional maps, which have been popularised for 3D shape matching due to their powerful spectral formalism utilising an efficient low-dimensional linear representation. However, functional maps require that domains (in our cases the rectangular image grids) are equipped with an informative and non-trivial geometry. To define a meaningful manifold structure for images, we use Galerkin's method from finite elements to derive a discrete Laplace-Beltrami operator (LBO) based on a manifold embedding of deep image features. Further, we leverage a neural adjoint map that allows to represent non-linear mappings. We demonstrate that our method sets the new state of the art among zero-shot image correspondence methods on multiple dense correspondence benchmarks of real-world images. Our code is publicly available: this https URL

AI.tldr: The paper applies functional maps to zero-shot image correspondence by building a Laplace-Beltrami operator from a manifold embedding of deep image features and using a neural adjoint map, reaching state-of-the-art dense correspondence on real-image benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Nearest-neighbour matching of foundation model features gives noisy dense correspondences between instances of similar categories, and functional maps need the image grid to have an informative geometry, which images lack by default.
AI.method: Galerkin's method from finite elements derives a discrete Laplace-Beltrami operator from a manifold embedding of deep features, and a neural adjoint map represents non-linear mappings between the functional spaces.
AI.result: The method sets a new state of the art among zero-shot image correspondence methods on multiple dense correspondence benchmarks of real-world images; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Regularising matching through a spectral, feature-derived image geometry improves zero-shot semantic correspondence.

title: Sparse Anchors for Visual Multi-Session Registration in Changing Environments
summary: Repeated robotic monitoring requires localization across visits to the same environment, even if the environment changes. Such changes can substantially reduce persistent visual content, and repetitive structures can lead to incorrect cross-session correspondences. In this paper, we address visual multi-session registration of a new data recording (the query session) to a previously reconstructed reference map. Under substantial visual and structural changes, cross-session localization may be possible only for parts of the trajectory. In our approach, we therefore rely on a sparse set of reliable absolute pose constraints and combine them with within-session relative-pose information to register the complete trajectory to the reference map. We first estimate absolute alignment hypotheses through visual place recognition, local feature matching, and geometric verification. We then use sequence consensus to reject hypotheses that are inconsistent with a common query-to-reference alignment and retain the remaining poses as absolute anchors. These anchors are refined through featuremetric alignment against a Gaussian feature field and combined with within-session relative-pose constraints in a robust pose-graph optimization. We evaluate our approach on 15 cross-session experiments from the challenging HILTI26 construction-site dataset, covering substantial scene changes and difficult-to-match environments. Our method achieves 94.4% recall within 1m and 100.0% within 5m, outperforming independent image localization, which peaks at 65.3% and 70.7%, respectively, as well as direct registration of independently reconstructed Structure-from-Motion geometry. Our results show that sparse, reliable absolute anchors can provide accurate and complete trajectory registration even when reliable cross-session correspondences are available only for part of the query session.

AI.tldr: The paper registers a new recording to a reference map under environmental change using sparse, reliable absolute pose anchors chosen by sequence consensus and combined with relative poses in a robust pose graph, reaching 94.4% recall within 1 m on HILTI26.
AI.motivation: Repeated robotic monitoring must localise against changed environments where persistent visual content is reduced and repetitive structure causes wrong cross-session matches, so only part of a trajectory may localise reliably.
AI.method: Absolute alignment hypotheses come from visual place recognition, local feature matching and geometric verification, sequence consensus rejects inconsistent hypotheses, the remaining anchors are refined by featuremetric alignment against a Gaussian feature field, and they are fused with within-session relative poses in pose-graph optimisation.
AI.result: On 15 cross-session experiments from the HILTI26 construction-site dataset the method achieves 94.4% recall within 1 m and 100.0% within 5 m, versus at most 65.3% and 70.7% for independent image localisation, and outperforms direct registration of independently reconstructed SfM geometry.
AI.conclusion: Sparse reliable anchors can give accurate and complete trajectory registration even when cross-session correspondences exist only for part of the query session.

title: Characterizing the vertical continuity of fuel strata based on TLS point clouds Gaussian decomposition and overlap metrics
comment: 45 pages, 15 figures Author affiliations and ORCID: Jesús Torralba this https URL , Luis Á. Ruiz this https URL , Pablo Crespo-Peremarch this https URL , Marina Simó-Martí this https URL , Juan Pedro Carbonell-Rivera this https URL
summary: Vertical forest structure influences fire behavior by regulating understory-to-canopy fuel connectivity, yet operational fuel-type models represent this complexity through discrete classes that only indirectly capture vertical continuity. High-density point clouds offer an opportunity to characterize vertical fuel connectivity in a more explicit and continuous manner, but specific methodological approaches are still required. We applied Gaussian decomposition to vertical height profiles derived from terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) point clouds across 25 permanent forest plots to characterize geometric vertical fuel continuity. A multiscale analysis spanning from the plot scale to ~0.5 $m^2$ units was used to evaluate geometric, probabilistic, and overlap metrics for characterizing fuel strata. The method reproduced the vertical transition between shrub and tree strata, with median Pearson correlations ranging from 0.83 to 0.96 across analysis levels. Probability density overlap metrics and separability indicators, such as the Jeffries-Matusita distance, provided complementary descriptors of vertical continuity. Intermediate spatial scales (3-6 m cells) provided a useful compromise between spatial detail and the consistent representation of shrub-canopy interaction patterns. Finer scales increased variability due to point density reduction and profile irregularity, and low mean squared error values were found insufficient as sole performance indicators. Gaussian decomposition applied to TLS point clouds enables explicit quantification of vertical fuel continuity, a limitation of current discrete classification systems. Continuous vertical connectivity metrics derived from this approach offer a pathway for improving ladder fuel characterization and strengthening decision-making support in wildfire risk assessment.

AI.tldr: The paper uses Gaussian decomposition of vertical height profiles from TLS point clouds across 25 forest plots to quantify vertical fuel continuity, and finds that intermediate 3-6 m cells best balance spatial detail and consistency.
AI.motivation: Operational fuel-type models describe vertical forest structure with discrete classes that only indirectly capture vertical fuel continuity, which affects how fire moves from understorey to canopy.
AI.method: Gaussian decomposition is applied to TLS vertical height profiles at multiple scales from plot level to about 0.5 m squared units, and geometric, probabilistic and overlap metrics, including the Jeffries-Matusita distance, are evaluated for fuel strata.
AI.result: The method reproduces the shrub-to-tree stratum transition with median Pearson correlations of 0.83 to 0.96 across analysis levels; intermediate 3-6 m cells give a useful compromise; finer scales increase variability, and low mean squared error alone is insufficient as a performance indicator.
AI.conclusion: Gaussian decomposition of TLS data gives explicit, continuous metrics of vertical fuel connectivity that could improve ladder fuel characterisation and wildfire risk assessment.

title: High-fidelity training-free photovoltaic module mapping from multi-view UAV imagery
summary: High-fidelity photovoltaic (PV) module mapping requires complete instance recovery and accurate delineation. Vision foundation models offer zero-shot segmentation, but converting incomplete and inconsistent predictions across views into a complete, geometrically accurate map of individual modules remains challenging. We propose the Multi-View PV Module Mapper (MV-PVMapper), a training-free framework coupling vision foundation models with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry. First, Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) generates candidates from original images using text prompts. Their contours are then transferred into object space through per-module slope correction to limit distortion from surface-model noise, and verified against representative module dimensions to guide cross-view instance selection. Finally, accepted instances return to all covering images as box prompts for SAM~3, supplementing text prompts with spatial cues for iterative segmentation, verification and fusion. On five-direction surveys of three operational rooftop PV plants at approximately 1 cm nadir ground sampling distance, two feedback iterations recover 7,710 of 7,711 reference modules with no false positives at an intersection-over-union (IoU) matching threshold of 0.5. Macro-averaged area precision and recall reach 99.00 % and 98.52 %, respectively. Averaged across sites, the aggregated Jaccard index reaches 97.55 %, compared with 60.73 % and 41.24 % for orthomosaic segmentation and multi-view pixel-voting baselines, respectively; average precision at the stricter IoU threshold of 0.95 reaches 95.67 %. Ablation studies show that module-size constraints are critical for instance separation, while slope correction and feedback to all covering views improve boundary accuracy. These results are achieved without task-specific image annotation or segmentation-model weight updates.

AI.tldr: MV-PVMapper maps individual photovoltaic modules from multi-view UAV imagery without training, combining SAM 3 with slope-corrected geometry and cross-view feedback, recovering 7,710 of 7,711 reference modules with no false positives.
AI.motivation: Accurate PV module mapping needs complete instance recovery and accurate boundaries, but zero-shot segmentation predictions are incomplete and inconsistent across views, and orthomosaic or pixel-voting baselines are inadequate.
AI.method: SAM 3 generates text-prompted candidates per image, contours are transferred to object space with per-module slope correction and checked against module dimensions for cross-view selection, and accepted instances return as box prompts to all covering images for iterative segmentation and fusion.
AI.result: Over five-direction surveys of three rooftop PV plants at about 1 cm GSD, two feedback iterations recover 7,710 of 7,711 modules with no false positives at IoU 0.5; macro-averaged area precision and recall are 99.00% and 98.52%; aggregated Jaccard index is 97.55% versus 60.73% and 41.24% for the baselines, and AP at IoU 0.95 is 95.67%.
AI.conclusion: Combining foundation-model segmentation with photogrammetric geometry and multi-view feedback yields accurate PV module maps without task-specific annotation or weight updates.

title: When Cell Crops Share a Parent: Measuring and Isolating Acquisition Leakage in Cervical Cytology Benchmarks
summary: Public cervical cytology benchmarks release many cell crops cut from far fewer microscope fields or slides and are often split at the crop level, so test cells share acquisition parents with training cells. In a preregistered study, crop-level splitting raised SIPaKMeD accuracy by 0.97 percentage points across twelve architectures and twenty seeds (95% CI 0.59-1.39), and CRIC accuracy by 12.08 points (11.16-12.99). On SIPaKMeD, a factorial that fixes training crop and parent counts attributes the gain to sibling exposure (1.73 points, 0.95-2.51), not to the extra parent diversity of crop-level splits (0.00). Parent identity is decodable at about 100 times chance, yet erasing 82% of its above-floor linear recoverability left the gap unchanged, and Grad-CAM did not distinguish leaking from clean models; matching test cells' color statistics to an unseen same-class field removed most of the advantage. Decodability and saliency cannot substitute for a parent-disjoint split.

AI.tldr: Crop-level splitting of cervical cytology benchmarks leaks acquisition parents between training and test, inflating accuracy by about 1 point on SIPaKMeD and 12 points on CRIC, and this comes from sibling exposure rather than parent diversity.
AI.motivation: Public benchmarks release many cell crops from few fields or slides and split at crop level, so test cells share acquisition parents with training cells, which may inflate reported performance.
AI.method: In a preregistered study across twelve architectures and twenty seeds, crop-level and parent-disjoint splits were compared, a factorial design fixing training crop and parent counts isolated sibling exposure, and parent decodability, feature erasure, Grad-CAM and colour-statistics matching were analysed.
AI.result: Crop-level splitting raised SIPaKMeD accuracy by 0.97 points (95% CI 0.59 to 1.39) and CRIC accuracy by 12.08 points; sibling exposure accounts for 1.73 points on SIPaKMeD while extra parent diversity contributes 0.00; parent identity is decodable at about 100 times chance, but erasing 82% of its recoverability left the gap unchanged, and matching colour statistics removed most of the advantage.
AI.conclusion: Decodability and saliency cannot substitute for a parent-disjoint split, which is needed for valid cervical cytology benchmarking.

title: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding
summary: Vision-language verifiers judge whether an image faithfully matches a textual description, yet existing training pipelines typically rely on static supervision from stronger external judges or curated hard-negative data. Such supervision requires external generation or annotation, is teacher-bounded, and is difficult to adapt as model failures evolve. We introduce PROVE (Perturb-and-Repair Optimization for Vision-Language Evaluation), a self-play framework that trains verifiers through a closed perturb-verify-repair-verify loop. Starting from a known-correct image-caption pair, a Mutator introduces a typed perturbation over objects, attributes, counts, or relations. The verifier then judges the perturbed caption and provides textual feedback, which a Repairer uses to recover a faithful caption for re-verification. These two verification rounds produce structured rewards for informative mismatches and visually grounded repairs. Since perturbation, verification, and repair are role-conditioned behaviors of the same evolving multimodal backbone, updating the shared parameters also improves the verifier itself. Experiments show that PROVE improves fine-grained compositional verification across model scales and families and strengthens visual-detail robustness on the reference backbone, with limited, benchmark-dependent changes on broader multimodal tasks.

AI.tldr: PROVE is a self-play framework that trains vision-language verifiers by perturbing a correct caption, verifying it, repairing it and verifying again, using the same evolving backbone for all roles, with gains in compositional verification.
AI.motivation: Verifier training usually depends on static supervision from stronger external judges or curated hard negatives, which is teacher-bounded, costly to produce and hard to keep up with evolving failures.
AI.method: Starting from a known-correct image-caption pair, a Mutator introduces a typed perturbation over objects, attributes, counts or relations, the verifier judges the perturbed caption and gives textual feedback, and a Repairer recovers a faithful caption; the two verification rounds give structured rewards, and all roles share the same parameters.
AI.result: PROVE improves fine-grained compositional verification across model scales and families and strengthens visual-detail robustness on the reference backbone, with limited and benchmark-dependent changes on broader multimodal tasks.
AI.conclusion: Closed-loop self-play can improve verifiers without external judges, though the benefit on broader multimodal tasks is modest.

title: PadLoc: Training-Free Floor-Plan Localization by Sparse Geometric Matching
comment: Accepted to WACV 2027 (Algorithms track). 22 pages: main paper (10 pages incl. references) and supplementary material (12 pages). Code: this https URL
summary: We propose PadLoc, a training-free localization back-end that places a moving sensor within a known floor plan. Floor plans are cheap, persistent, and robust to appearance change, but recent learned-depth methods localize against them by filtering per-frame depth through dense $(x,y,\theta)$ pose grids. PadLoc keeps the swappable depth front-end and replaces the dense grid back-end with sparse geometric matching: dominant wall orientations define a small pose-candidate set, masked normalized cross-correlation scores observed free space against the plan, and a moving-pose Gaussian-mixture Bayes filter plus consensus readout decodes the trajectory. Holding each competitor's depth fixed, PadLoc matches or beats UnLoc's forward filter and the F3Loc filter at every Gibson trajectory length, and UnLoc's offline refinement from $T=35$ on; it exceeds Z-FLoc's published results with a shared MapAnything front-end. On Bonn LiLocBench, PadLoc improves pooled SR@1m over UnLoc by 23-32 pp under wheel odometry and 35-43 pp with ground-truth motion; with full-FOV LiDAR plus wheel odometry the same readout reaches 100% SR@1m at 9-10 cm median error on the static sequence. On the Hilti-Trimble Localization Challenge PadLoc localizes a camera-only fisheye rig on construction floors hundreds of metres across at 0.90-0.98 online SR@2m on three of five sessions; adding learned wall isolation, applied to every session, covers all five at 0.67-0.92 with the localizer unchanged throughout. PadLoc thus matches or outperforms dense grid back-ends while preserving sensor modularity and a compact state that does not grow with trajectory length.

AI.tldr: PadLoc localises a moving sensor in a known floor plan without training, replacing dense pose grids with sparse geometric matching over dominant wall orientations, and matches or beats prior back-ends on Gibson, Bonn LiLocBench and Hilti-Trimble data.
AI.motivation: Floor-plan localisation with learned depth filters per-frame depth through dense (x, y, theta) grids, which is costly and grows with trajectory length in its compact state representation.
AI.method: Dominant wall orientations define a small pose-candidate set, masked normalised cross-correlation scores observed free space against the plan, and a moving-pose Gaussian-mixture Bayes filter with a consensus readout decodes the trajectory, with the depth front-end kept swappable.
AI.result: With a fixed depth front-end PadLoc matches or beats UnLoc's forward filter and the F3Loc filter at every Gibson trajectory length; on Bonn LiLocBench it improves pooled SR@1m over UnLoc by 23-32 points with wheel odometry and 35-43 points with ground-truth motion; with full-FOV LiDAR and wheel odometry it reaches 100% SR@1m at 9-10 cm median error on the static sequence; on Hilti-Trimble, online SR@2m is 0.90-0.98 on three of five sessions and 0.67-0.92 on all five with learned wall isolation.
AI.conclusion: Sparse geometric matching matches or outperforms dense grid back-ends while keeping sensor modularity and a compact state that does not grow with trajectory length.

title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
summary: Transfer learning from natural images is standard in supervised and increasingly adopted in self-supervised medical image analysis, but its role in generative modelling, and in particular diffusion denoisers, remains underexplored. Medical diffusion models typically train the denoiser from scratch, with no systematic evaluation of natural-image transfer. We analyse this across latent and pixel paradigms, model sizes (131M-952M) and two radiology datasets (RadImageNet, BraTS), and ask which aspects of transfer support generation. We find that: i) Natural-image initialisation consistently improves generation, by 21-34% relative gFID in pixel space against 14% in latent space, where the tokeniser supplies much of the prior. gFID gains mirror downstream pathology classification and radiomic-feature FD, both proxies for clinical fidelity. ii) Benefits reflect spatial structure, not semantics: semantic probing does not predict generation quality, whereas a spatial-structure metric adapted to internal denoiser representations tracks gFID at $|r|=0.85$, positioning spatial organisation as a channel through which pretraining manifests. iii) Mixed-domain denoiser training shows that natural and medical images share similar layer-wise representations up to the late blocks, and mixing natural images into medical training improves fidelity. iv) Transfer benefit is tied to natural image initialisation, outperforming in-domain medical pretraining and several reinitialisation schemes. Overall, natural image denoisers transfer positively to medical ones in our setup. Code is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: The paper tests whether natural-image pretraining helps diffusion denoisers for medical image generation and finds that it consistently improves generation quality, with the benefit tied to spatial structure rather than semantics.
AI.motivation: Medical diffusion models usually train the denoiser from scratch, and the role of natural-image transfer in generative modelling, unlike supervised or self-supervised medical analysis, has not been systematically evaluated.
AI.method: The authors compare latent and pixel diffusion paradigms with model sizes from 131M to 952M parameters on RadImageNet and BraTS, and examine initialisation, a spatial-structure metric on internal denoiser representations, layer-wise representation similarity, mixed-domain training, and reinitialisation schemes.
AI.result: Natural-image initialisation improves gFID by 21-34% relative in pixel space and 14% in latent space, and gFID gains track pathology classification and radiomic-feature FD. A spatial-structure metric tracks gFID with |r| = 0.85, semantic probing does not predict generation quality, and mixing natural images into medical training improves fidelity; natural-image initialisation outperforms in-domain medical pretraining and several reinitialisation schemes.
AI.conclusion: Natural-image denoisers transfer positively to medical image generation in this setup, and spatial organisation is identified as the channel through which pretraining helps.

title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
comment: Project page: this https URL, Code: this https URL
summary: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications. In this work, we introduce Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which decouples compositional query comprehension from building discriminative embeddings. Rather than directly projecting the composed query into a single embedding without internal reasoning, FactEmbed employs a set of factorized latents that simulate the intended visual modifications via an intermediate target imagination objective. This process encourages the latents to ground into target semantics before forming discriminative representations for retrieval. Subsequently, to propagate these factorized representations throughout the model for retrieval, we optimize a factor-level contrastive loss while distilling the decomposed representations into a deeper attention layer of the MLLM. Finally, for efficient inference, we retain the [EOS] token to establish a global-level embedding on top of these factorized latents, while we exploit the mean-pooled factorized latents to rerank a short candidate list at negligible cost, as both are produced by the same forward pass. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that FactEmbed outperforms prior works across CIR benchmarks.

AI.tldr: FactEmbed is a composed image retrieval method that factorises MLLM query embeddings into latents that simulate the intended visual modification before forming discriminative retrieval embeddings.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLM-based composed image retrieval methods map the reference image and modification text directly to an embedding through contrastive supervision, which leaves the MLLM's compositional understanding underused because the intended visual modifications are never resolved explicitly.
AI.method: FactEmbed uses a set of factorised latents trained with a target imagination objective to ground into target semantics, a factor-level contrastive loss, distillation of the decomposed representations into a deeper attention layer, and an inference scheme that combines the [EOS] global embedding with mean-pooled factorised latents for reranking a short candidate list.
AI.result: The abstract reports that FactEmbed outperforms prior works across composed image retrieval benchmarks, without giving specific numbers in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly factorising compositional query comprehension from embedding construction is presented as a practical way to better exploit MLLMs for composed image retrieval at negligible extra inference cost.

title: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data
summary: Accurate vegetation-encroachment assessment and risk mitigation require electric utilities to accurately locate and characterize distribution-network assets, including poles and power lines, and distinguish among medium-voltage, low-voltage, neutral, and telecommunication lines. Mobile and aerial Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds provide detailed 3D representations of these assets and their surroundings. However, power-line detection and reconstruction remain challenging because conductor returns are often sparse, incomplete, noisy, or occluded by vegetation. These challenges are especially significant in distribution networks, where lower pole heights and complex line configurations place conductors close to trees. In addition, mobile and aerial LiDAR datasets differ substantially in point density, viewing geometry, spatial coverage, and occlusion patterns. We propose a robust and automated reconstruction method combining scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting, and iterative fragment merging to recover individual conductors under severe data incompleteness and occlusion. Following semantic classification, the same reconstruction pipeline processes both mobile and aerial LiDAR data without modality-specific code or parameter tuning. The method is evaluated through degradation experiments, benchmarking, parameter sensitivity analysis, and large-scale validation. On the aerial dataset, it achieves 96.87% precision, 96.66% recall, a 96.76% F$_1$-score, and a geometric RMSE of 0.127 m. On the mobile dataset, where conductor-level reference annotations were unavailable, it achieves a point-to-model RMSE of 0.045 m and a reconstruction coverage of 95.27%. Source code, documentation, and evaluation data are publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an automated method that reconstructs individual power lines from incomplete mobile and aerial LiDAR point clouds using one pipeline with no modality-specific code or tuning.
AI.motivation: Power-line detection from LiDAR is hard because conductor returns are sparse, noisy and occluded by vegetation, and mobile and aerial LiDAR differ in density, geometry, coverage and occlusion patterns.
AI.method: The method combines scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting and iterative fragment merging after semantic classification, and applies the same pipeline to both mobile and aerial data.
AI.result: On the aerial dataset it achieves 96.87% precision, 96.66% recall, 96.76% F1-score and a geometric RMSE of 0.127 m; on the mobile dataset, without conductor-level reference annotations, it achieves a point-to-model RMSE of 0.045 m and 95.27% reconstruction coverage.
AI.conclusion: A single modality-agnostic reconstruction pipeline can recover conductors accurately under severe incompleteness and occlusion, supporting automated vegetation-encroachment assessment for electric utilities.

title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking
summary: Tracking-by-propagation (TBP) methods perform end-to-end multi-object tracking by propagating track queries across frames, jointly handling detection and identity association without heuristic post-processing while naturally modeling temporal information. However, as detection and association are tightly coupled, detection queries in TBP are expected to discover currently untracked objects and provide complementary current-frame evidence for challenging tracks whose queries and identities are retained. Existing methods largely inherit detection-query formation from single-frame detection and construct such queries before the decoder with little awareness of trajectory states. Consequently, currently untracked objects may be missed, while challenging tracked objects with reduced visibility under occlusion may lack complementary evidence, causing association failures or duplicate responses. To address these issues, we propose TAQ-MOTR, a tracking-aware detection query formation framework that employs a pre-decoder Hybrid Query Generator (HQG) to fuse current-frame image features, track memory, and learnable memory. By conditioning detection queries on trajectory states, TAQ-MOTR adapts them to \rev{the discovery of currently untracked objects and tracked-object complementation We further introduce a training-only auxiliary detection branch whose one-to-one label assignment is decoupled from that of the main tracking branch, providing additional detection supervision to strengthen the shared HQG and decoder for the discovery of currently untracked objects. TAQ-MOTR improves performance on DanceTrack, SportsMOT, and BFT, achieving 72.0 HOTA, 63.1 AssA, and 76.6 IDF1 on the DanceTrack test set. Code is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: TAQ-MOTR improves end-to-end multiple object tracking by conditioning detection queries on trajectory states through a pre-decoder Hybrid Query Generator and a training-only auxiliary detection branch.
AI.motivation: In tracking-by-propagation methods, detection queries are built as in single-frame detection with little awareness of track states, so currently untracked objects may be missed and occluded tracked objects may lack complementary evidence, causing association failures or duplicate responses.
AI.method: The Hybrid Query Generator fuses current-frame image features, track memory and learnable memory before the decoder, and a training-only auxiliary detection branch with its own one-to-one label assignment supplies extra detection supervision to the shared generator and decoder.
AI.result: TAQ-MOTR improves performance on DanceTrack, SportsMOT and BFT, and reaches 72.0 HOTA, 63.1 AssA and 76.6 IDF1 on the DanceTrack test set.
AI.conclusion: Trajectory-aware detection query formation is presented as a way to improve both discovery of untracked objects and association in end-to-end multi-object tracking.

title: Diffusion Plug-in Priors for Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration
summary: \textit{Objective:} Ultrasound videos are limited by hardware-constrained spatial resolution and signal-dependent speckle, while paired low- and high-resolution acquisitions for supervised restoration are rarely available. We aim to jointly super-resolve and despeckle ultrasound videos without paired training data or network retraining. \textit{Methods:} We propose UltraDiff, which uses a frozen pre-trained diffusion model (DM) as a plug-in prior and restores each frame by optimizing the latent seed of the DM sampler under a range-constrained maximum a posteriori formulation. We derive a speckle-aware data-fidelity term from a Rayleigh scale-family model and characterize its relative-residual and variance-adaptive weighting properties. We further introduce a stabilized fidelity that is bounded below and strictly convex in log intensity for positive observations in its unclamped form. A total-variation regularizer complements the DM prior, and a temporal seed update warm-starts each frame from the optimized seed of its predecessor. \textit{Results:} On EchoNet-LVH videos with simulated speckle and additive noise, UltraDiff with a natural-image prior improves PSNR by 1.24\,dB over the strongest baseline, and ultrasound-related priors improve it further. On real clinical echocardiography videos, UltraDiff reduces the mean absolute error of zero-shot ejection fraction (EF) prediction from 7.31 to 6.37 EF points relative to DUP, the strongest baseline. \textit{Conclusion:} Combining a speckle-aware fidelity with frozen diffusion priors enables ground-truth-free ultrasound video restoration that benefits downstream measurement. \textit{Significance:} UltraDiff needs neither paired data nor retraining and is not tied to a specific diffusion checkpoint. Code associated with this work will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: UltraDiff jointly super-resolves and despeckles ultrasound videos by optimising the latent seed of a frozen pretrained diffusion model as a prior, requiring no paired data and no retraining.
AI.motivation: Ultrasound videos suffer from hardware-limited resolution and signal-dependent speckle, and paired low- and high-resolution acquisitions for supervised restoration are rarely available.
AI.method: Each frame is restored by optimising the diffusion sampler's latent seed under a range-constrained MAP formulation, with a speckle-aware data-fidelity term derived from a Rayleigh scale-family model, a stabilised fidelity term, a total-variation regulariser, and a temporal seed update that warm-starts each frame from its predecessor.
AI.result: On EchoNet-LVH with simulated speckle and noise, UltraDiff with a natural-image prior improves PSNR by 1.24 dB over the strongest baseline, with ultrasound-related priors improving it further; on real echocardiography, it reduces zero-shot ejection fraction MAE from 7.31 to 6.37 EF points relative to DUP.
AI.conclusion: Frozen diffusion priors combined with a speckle-aware fidelity term enable ground-truth-free ultrasound video restoration that benefits downstream measurement, without dependence on a specific diffusion checkpoint.

title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions
summary: We introduce PLANTEUR, a benchmark for crop-type mapping from satellite images in the French overseas territories. Building on the PASTIS design, PLANTEUR provides georeferenced and aligned Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8 sequences with parcel-derived labels spanning six tropical regions and an 8-class label space. We define both a standard test split and a leave-one-island-out protocol to measure cross-territory generalization, and evaluate fully supervised models, linear probes, and fine-tuned foundation models. The benchmark code and data are open source and available on GitHub and Hugging Face.

AI.tldr: PLANTEUR is a benchmark for crop-type segmentation from satellite image time series in French tropical overseas territories, built on the PASTIS design.
AI.motivation: Crop-type mapping benchmarks are lacking for tropical regions, and generalisation across territories needs to be measured.
AI.method: The benchmark provides aligned Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1 and Landsat-8 sequences with parcel-derived labels over six tropical regions and an 8-class label space, with a standard test split and a leave-one-island-out protocol, and is evaluated with fully supervised models, linear probes and fine-tuned foundation models.
AI.result: The abstract does not report numerical results; it states that the benchmark code and data are open source on GitHub and Hugging Face.
AI.conclusion: PLANTEUR provides an open resource for evaluating cross-territory generalisation of crop-type segmentation in tropical regions.

title: Diagnosis by Composition: Detecting and Localizing Unseen Diseases by Composing Learned Radiological Findings
summary: Deep models for radiological diagnosis are typically trained to predict disease labels directly from images, which limits them to diseases seen during training and makes their decisions hard to interpret in radiologists' terms. Radiology, however, proceeds from visual findings to disease through published guidelines that make this decision rule explicit, interpretable, and reproducible. We introduce diagnosis by composition (DbC), a representation learning framework that encodes this findings-first logic. DbC learns a vocabulary of radiological findings by aligning image features with the text embeddings of the findings, each finding represented as a dense map over the scan. A disease is defined by a set of required findings derived from its guidelines, and its diagnosis map is a fixed, parameter-free composition of the corresponding finding maps. Because the finding-to-disease mapping is derived from guidelines rather than learned, DbC is interpretable and auditable by design, can extend to new diseases by specifying their findings without retraining, and can diagnose unseen diseases by composing their findings. On multi-phase liver CT, DbC detects and localizes unseen diseases, rare diseases from a different institution, and an external cohort significantly better than all comparators, including models that align images with disease names. DbC also improves detection and localization in the fully supervised setting and remains superior across training-set sizes. Although demonstrated on liver CT, DbC applies wherever radiological guidelines define diseases through findings.

AI.tldr: Diagnosis by Composition (DbC) detects and localises diseases, including unseen ones, by composing learned radiological finding maps according to guideline-derived finding-to-disease rules.
AI.motivation: Deep radiological classifiers predict disease labels directly from images, which restricts them to seen diseases and makes their decisions hard to interpret in radiologists' terms, whereas guidelines define diagnosis through visual findings.
AI.method: DbC learns a vocabulary of findings by aligning image features with finding text embeddings, each represented as a dense map over the scan, and defines a disease's diagnosis map as a fixed, parameter-free composition of its required finding maps taken from guidelines.
AI.result: On multi-phase liver CT, DbC detects and localises unseen diseases, rare diseases from another institution and an external cohort significantly better than all comparators, including models that align images with disease names, and it also improves detection and localisation in the fully supervised setting.
AI.conclusion: Guideline-derived composition of findings gives an interpretable, auditable framework that can extend to new diseases without retraining, and it applies wherever guidelines define diseases through findings.

title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems. We develop a unified theoretical foundation that characterizes optimal routing under quality--cost trade-offs and establishes how the information available to a router determines its attainable performance. To systematically investigate routing across diverse capabilities, we first construct an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks across language understanding, image, video, and speech generation, coding and workplace agents, and robotic manipulation, comprising 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations. Building on this framework, we train and test different routers to investigate the potential of omni-modal model routing, the capabilities of learned routers, and the conditions under which routing improves efficiency. Our results reveal substantial opportunities for capability orchestration: per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. More importantly, routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.

AI.tldr: Route Anything is a framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems, showing that routing over a large omni-modal candidate pool improves performance and efficiency.
AI.motivation: General-purpose AI would need orchestration of many specialised models, tools and policies, and it is unclear how a system should select the best candidate per task while balancing performance and cost.
AI.method: The authors develop a theoretical characterisation of optimal routing under quality-cost trade-offs, build an omni-modal trajectory matrix over 25 benchmarks with 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations, and train and test learned routers against oracle and fixed-candidate baselines.
AI.result: Per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time; routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average relative to the reference model.
AI.conclusion: Capability orchestration offers substantial gains, and the paper frames the information available to a router as determining its attainable performance.

title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
summary: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce Möbius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, Möbius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instruction-guided editing within a single model. On HumanML3D, Möbius achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified motion models. Scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data further demonstrates that our framework is both effective and scalable.

AI.tldr: Möbius is a unified motion-language model that performs motion understanding, generation and editing within one shared diffusion-based multimodal framework operating on raw continuous motion.
AI.motivation: Existing motion unified models only partially unify understanding and generation, since generation is usually delegated to a separate diffusion module over learned motion latents.
AI.method: Clean motion, noisy motion and text jointly participate in shared attention, with role-specific parameters for the understanding and generation streams, and the model operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion without discrete tokenisation or a pretrained motion VAE.
AI.result: On HumanML3D, Möbius achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified motion models, and scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data is reported to be effective and scalable.
AI.conclusion: A single diffusion-in-shared-representation formulation supports captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion and instruction-guided editing within one model.

title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) integrate visual understanding, generation, and editing within a single unified framework. However, existing unified multimodal datasets and benchmarks remain dominated by single-turn tasks. Even in recent multi-turn datasets, many turns can be solved independently without tracking information across turns. Consequently, they provide limited supervision and evaluation for multimodal stateful interaction, which requires models to understand, maintain, update, and faithfully realize evolving dialogue states across turns. To address this gap, we introduce YANAMI, the first large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark for stateful interaction, comprising YANAMI-400K and YANAMI-Bench. YANAMI-400K contains 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogues, with more than 2M images and 2.6M dialogue turns. The dialogues span four representative scenarios: Multi-Image Fusion, Image Editing, World Modeling, and Visual Reasoning, and require models to continuously track, preserve, and revise evolving multimodal dialogue states across turns. YANAMI-Bench comprises 400 multi-turn dialogues for systematically evaluating multimodal stateful interaction. It jointly evaluates Dialogue State Understanding and Visual Realization, characterizing the gap between models' ability to understand evolving dialogue states and their ability to faithfully realize them in visual outputs. Experiments show that fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improves image editing, generation, and multimodal stateful interaction by 10.3%, 2.0%, and 13.23%, respectively, while preserving its general visual understanding capabilities. Evaluations on YANAMI-Bench further reveal that existing UMMs still struggle to maintain, update, and visually realize evolving multimodal dialogue states.

AI.tldr: YANAMI provides a large-scale multimodal dataset and benchmark for multi-turn stateful interaction in unified multimodal models, where earlier dialogue states must be tracked and faithfully realised visually.
AI.motivation: Existing unified multimodal datasets are dominated by single-turn tasks, and even multi-turn ones often allow each turn to be solved without tracking earlier information.
AI.method: YANAMI-400K contains 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogues with over 2M images and 2.6M turns across Multi-Image Fusion, Image Editing, World Modeling and Visual Reasoning scenarios, and YANAMI-Bench contains 400 dialogues that jointly evaluate Dialogue State Understanding and Visual Realization.
AI.result: Fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improves image editing by 10.3%, generation by 2.0% and multimodal stateful interaction by 13.23%, while preserving general visual understanding; existing UMMs still struggle on YANAMI-Bench.
AI.conclusion: Stateful multi-turn multimodal interaction is a remaining weakness of current unified models, and the dataset and benchmark provide supervision and evaluation for it.

title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an imperceptible budget of 1/255, SuperVLAD and BoQ keep at most 0.2% top-1 recall (R@1) on four benchmarks. We propose anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT), which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive and an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model. Checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance, and the full trade-off is reported. Within five validation R@1 points of clean cost, plain adversarial training has no admissible checkpoint, whereas ARAFT raises robust R@1 from zero to 47.3 on SuperVLAD and 55.3 on BoQ; plain adversarial training exceeds this only at about three times the clean cost. Against unbudgeted plain adversarial training on the test sets, ARAFT matches its robust R@1 at 2/255 with about ten more clean R@1 points. At 4/255, plain adversarial training is 6-9 robust R@1 points ahead, while ARAFT still keeps its ten-point clean advantage. Developed on SuperVLAD, ARAFT transfers to BoQ without re-tuning, and its robustness holds against stronger optimisers, with no sign of gradient masking.

AI.tldr: ARAFT fine-tunes a pretrained visual place recognition model with an anchored listwise rank-adversarial loss, achieving much higher robust recall than plain adversarial training at a fixed clean-accuracy budget.
AI.motivation: Foundation-model visual place recognition models are accurate but very vulnerable to white-box ranking attacks, with SuperVLAD and BoQ keeping at most 0.2% top-1 recall under a 1/255 budget.
AI.method: ARAFT fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive, plus an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model, and checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance.
AI.result: Within five validation R@1 points of clean cost, plain adversarial training has no admissible checkpoint, whereas ARAFT raises robust R@1 from zero to 47.3 on SuperVLAD and 55.3 on BoQ; at 4/255 plain adversarial training is 6-9 robust R@1 points ahead, while ARAFT keeps a ten-point clean advantage, and ARAFT transfers to BoQ without re-tuning.
AI.conclusion: ARAFT offers a better robustness-accuracy trade-off for pretrained place recognition models, and its robustness holds against stronger optimisers without signs of gradient masking.

title: Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification
summary: 3D point cloud classification, a task in computer vision, has recently gained substantial interest due to its extensive applications across various domains such as augmented and virtual reality, robotics, and autonomous driving. However, classifying 3D point clouds becomes challenging in real-world scenarios where the density levels vary. These variations are due to limitations inherent to current sensing technologies and variable environmental conditions, which often prevent the capture of detailed and comprehensive geometric representations. Existing classification methods, which have demonstrated impressive results on dense point clouds, may be affected and could experience reduced performance when dealing with low-density point clouds. Addressing this challenge, this paper introduces LD-PointNet++, an architecture optimized for the classification of low-density point clouds. To pave the way for LD-PointNet++, we conduct the first benchmarking study that systematically evaluates state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods across varying densities, revealing significant performance declines in low-density environments. Experimental results on the ModelNet benchmark dataset demonstrate that LD-PointNet++ not only outperforms these methods in low-density scenarios but also demonstrates consistent accuracy above 90% across different density levels.

AI.tldr: LD-PointNet++ is a point cloud classification architecture designed for low-density inputs, supported by the first systematic benchmark of state-of-the-art classifiers across point densities.
AI.motivation: Point cloud classifiers that perform well on dense data degrade on low-density point clouds that arise from sensing limitations and environmental conditions, and this regime had not been systematically benchmarked.
AI.method: The authors benchmark state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods across varying densities and then propose LD-PointNet++, an architecture optimised for low-density classification.
AI.result: Benchmarking reveals significant performance declines at low density, and on ModelNet LD-PointNet++ outperforms these methods in low-density scenarios and keeps accuracy above 90% across density levels.
AI.conclusion: Architectures designed for low-density point clouds can keep high classification accuracy where existing methods degrade, which matters for applications such as AR/VR, robotics and autonomous driving.

title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
comment: Full version will be released soon
summary: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other. Exist- ing models describe the whole image with one description, so they cannot say where each correction belongs. To solve this problem, we present Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for image quality enhancement. It corrects several defects of a real photograph at the same time, each in the region where it occurs. Every block of the model holds a mixture of N = 13 experts. A router, trained with the model, sends every image patch to k = 5 of them. No degradation classifier, mask, prompt, detector, or task label is used. Another issue is that standard MoE training, taken from language models, pushes every expert toward equal use. Equal use applies every correction everywhere, even where it is not needed. We replace this rule with a bias that only sets a minimum share of use. Across all patches, an expert used less than this minimum gets higher router scores until it is selected again. An expert above the minimum is not changed, so no expert is forced to be used as often as the others. The bias needs no extra loss. The method adds no extra module and no extra processing step. We evaluate Wonder 4 on DIV2K and Flickr2K, against five published methods and three open-weight pipelines. It reaches the best LPIPS, DISTS, and NIQE on all three test settings (DIV2K x4, DIV2K x8, and Flickr2K x4).

AI.tldr: Wonder 4 is a mixture-of-experts image quality enhancement model that corrects several degradations of real photographs region by region, using a router with a minimum-usage bias instead of an equal-usage load-balancing loss.
AI.motivation: Real photographs combine blur, grain, compression, scratches and low resolution with conflicting corrections, and existing models apply one description to the whole image, so they cannot localise where each correction belongs.
AI.method: Each block holds a mixture of N = 13 experts, and a router trained with the model sends each image patch to k = 5 of them without degradation classifiers, masks or prompts; standard equal-usage MoE balancing is replaced by a bias that only raises the router scores of experts used below a minimum share, requiring no extra loss or module.
AI.result: On DIV2K and Flickr2K, compared with five published methods and three open-weight pipelines, Wonder 4 reaches the best LPIPS, DISTS and NIQE on all three test settings (DIV2K x4, DIV2K x8 and Flickr2K x4).
AI.conclusion: Region-wise routing with a minimum-usage constraint is presented as an effective way to apply different restoration corrections where they are needed, rather than uniformly across the image.

title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations and Datasets Track. Dataset: this https URL code: this https URL
summary: Automatic tools can now generate whole-brain MRI parcellations at cohort scale, but generated-label releases often provide little evidence about which cases are reliable enough to reuse. We introduce OpenBrain, a confidence-aware release of 35,838 provenance-verified OpenNeuro T1w cases from 607 source datasets. OpenBrain is organized as an auditable case-record release rather than a directory of standalone segmentation files: each record links a primary parcellation, two committee parcellations, source/license provenance, raw QC-7 measurements, percentile risks, a combined risk score R, and a confidence tier. QC-7 is a reference-free reliability panel over label geometry, image-label consistency, and committee disagreement, so users can filter, weight, audit, or re-threshold generated labels without rerunning inference. We evaluate this released evidence under a frozen protocol. Across external cohorts, lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality; in fixed-budget training, lower-risk selections improve paired macro Dice over random selection by +3.2 to +3.7 percentage points. OpenBrain also exposes raw axes, committee outputs, provenance, and datasheet documentation, so confidence claims remain inspectable after download. It does not turn generated labels into manual annotations or clinical-grade segmentations. Its contribution is a large open generated-parcellation substrate, a reusable case-level risk-evidence layer, and an external validation protocol for release-time QC. Dataset: this https URL. Code: this https URL.

AI.tldr: OpenBrain is an auditable release of 35,838 generated whole-brain MRI parcellations with per-case provenance, committee outputs and a confidence-tier risk score, enabling users to filter generated labels without rerunning inference.
AI.motivation: Automatic whole-brain parcellation tools can now be run at cohort scale, but generated-label releases rarely indicate which cases are reliable enough to reuse.
AI.method: Each record links a primary parcellation, two committee parcellations, source and licence provenance, raw QC-7 measurements, percentile risks, a combined risk score R and a confidence tier, where QC-7 is a reference-free reliability panel over label geometry, image-label consistency and committee disagreement.
AI.result: Across external cohorts, lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality, and in fixed-budget training lower-risk selections improve paired macro Dice over random selection by 3.2 to 3.7 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: OpenBrain offers a large open generated-parcellation resource, a reusable case-level risk layer and an external validation protocol for release-time QC, while not being presented as manual or clinical-grade segmentation.

title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs
summary: This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline for 3D {G}aussian {S}platting (GS) sequences {C}ompression with standard {V}ideo codecs. To meet the requirements of low-complexity and hardware compatibility from the industry, GSCV++ jointly improves preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping, and practical video compression configuration of GS compression. First, for preprocessing, energy-adaptive inter-frame spherical harmonic (SH) alternative current (AC) dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) is proposed to produces a compact and stable temporal SH AC feature space. It can reduce the data volume of following mapping and practical compression, as well as less complexity while eliminating redundant information. Second, for 3D-to-2D mapping, prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS (P-MiniPLAS) is designed to generate smooth 2D feature maps through prior-based weighting factor inference and small scale remapping. Compared with vanilla Parallel Linear Assignment Sorting (PLAS) and Morton scan, P-MiniPLAS ensures the generated 2D maps are more suitable for the video codec while maintaining a low level of computational complexity. Third, for practical compression, content-aware generalized compression (CA-GC) is developed to use a non-uniform bit-depth split for coordinate map generation, and a coding unit size selection is introduced for efficient compression complexity control, which fully exploits the performance of video codecs without involving normative changes. Experiments demonstrate that GSCV++ reports over 20\% in intra- and 60\% in inter-prediction rate-distortion gains compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. GSCV++ also achieves faster 2D map generation, encoding, and decoding than other SOTA methods using the same type of video codecs. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed modules and provide insights for subsequent research.

AI.tldr: GSCV++ compresses 3D Gaussian Splatting sequences with standard video codecs through improved preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping and codec configuration, aiming at low complexity and hardware compatibility.
AI.motivation: Industry needs low-complexity, hardware-compatible compression of Gaussian Splatting sequences, and existing pipelines spend substantial data and complexity on redundant temporal spherical harmonic information and on less suitable 2D mappings.
AI.method: Energy-adaptive inter-frame spherical harmonic AC dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) builds a compact temporal feature space, prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS (P-MiniPLAS) generates smooth 2D feature maps for the codec, and content-aware generalised compression (CA-GC) uses a non-uniform bit-depth split for coordinate maps and coding unit size selection without normative codec changes.
